text:
**The evidence does not establish whether the 2021 tree-cover loss was illegal.** Satellite data show 81.3 hectares of loss, and 98% of that area was mapped as forest in 2020.

Uruguay’s 2021 forest map classifies 68.1 hectares of the loss area as planted pine forest, none as native forest, and 13.2 hectares as outside mapped forest. This is consistent with possible plantation harvesting, but the imagery and maps do not establish the cause or legality of the loss.

A legal determination would require checking applicable rules, permits and land-management records.
